description: baseline

Target the n=32 launch-bound case by replacing the generated tiny warp scalar kernel with a single persistent block that factors multiple matrices per CTA and writes compact H/tau without per-matrix kernel scheduling overhead.

Packed the n=32 warp-per-matrix QR path four matrices per CTA; correctness passed but full geomean regressed to 2256.657629, likely from lower tiny-shape latency not offsetting block/occupancy effects elsewhere/noise.
Tried a less aggressive two-matrices-per-CTA tiny path; validation passed, but geomean was 2256.983972 and n=32 stayed around 10.28us, so CTA packing does not beat the baseline one-warp spread.
Completed the CTA-packing sweep with eight matrices per CTA; validation passed but geomean regressed further to 2257.857396 and n=32 was 10.327us, confirming this direction is not beneficial.

Implemented the brief literally: one 20-warp CTA handles the full n=32 batch. Validation passed, but n=32 slowed to 16.439us and geomean regressed to 2347.603403, so preserving many CTAs is more important than reducing block scheduling events.

Restored the original one-warp-per-matrix tiny launch after the persistent/packed CTA sweep regressed. Validation passed; benchmark measured 2257.160179 in this noisy run, but this is the best known design from the brief because all packed variants were slower, especially the literal one-CTA batch.

Brief exhausted. Tried packing the n=32 warp-per-matrix QR into 4, 2, 8, and literal 20-warps-per-CTA persistent-block launches. All variants validated but all regressed: 4 CTA-pack=2256.657629, 2=2256.983972, 8=2257.857396, and one-CTA batch=2347.603403 with n=32 slowing to 16.439us. Restored the original one-warp-per-matrix launch on final commit 89648414d5e075482be07054a53c817ac3d00ecc and captured an nsys profile for it; recommendation is not to pursue CTA packing for tiny QR because preserving per-matrix CTA spread/latency beats reducing block scheduling overhead.

Target the tiny n=32 case from baseline with the opposite strategy: keep one warp per matrix but fuse the Python/C++ dispatch overhead by routing n=32 through a dedicated extension entry that skips all runtime setters, tuple allocation branches, and generic blocked_qr_tiny setup.

Added blocked_qr_tiny32 and routed custom_kernel n<=32 directly to it, skipping generic dispatch and runtime tiny branches. Validation passed; n=32 measured 10.282us, full geomean 2256.855215, so the direct C++ entry did not beat baseline in the full active set.

Added a Python-level early return for n<=32 to existing blocked_qr_tiny, skipping the generic arm tuple/lambda loop while leaving C++ untouched. Validation passed; full geomean improved over the direct C++ entry to 2254.142686, but remained above parent.

Refined the Python fast path with a local bound extension method and data.size(1)==32. Validation passed, but geomean regressed to 2258.194143, so this lookup tweak was worse than the simpler data.shape fast path.

Restored the best simple Python fast path after local-binding regressed. Validation passed; remeasure gave 2255.680993 (prior same-code run was 2254.142686), still not a parent improvement but best within this brief.

Brief exhausted. Explored n=32 dispatch-overhead reductions while keeping one warp per matrix: (1) a dedicated C++ blocked_qr_tiny32 entry plus Python early route validated but measured 2256.855215; (2) a simpler Python early route to existing blocked_qr_tiny was best, 2254.142686 first run and 2255.680993 final remeasure; (3) local-bound method plus data.size(1)==32 regressed to 2258.194143. Final commit 5dcf32c22cba46f0e4861c77f2c2a1d07368aa51 keeps the simple Python fast path and has an nsys profile. None beat parent metric 2251.432; recommendation: dispatch shaving is below benchmark noise / dominated by allocation+launch, so next briefs should target allocation/return representation or checker interaction, not more Python/C++ branch trimming.

Target launch/allocation overhead across n=32 and small n=176/352 from baseline by changing the extension return representation: allocate one packed H/tau workspace per call, return views from it, and delete redundant scratch/tuple allocations in blocked_qr_tiny and blocked_qr.

Packed H/tau into one return buffer for blocked_qr and removed the dead unfused branch in blocked_qr_tiny. Validation passed, but full geomean was 2255.342777; n=176/352 worsened, likely because H.copy_(A) replaces the optimized contiguous().clone() path and view/narrow overhead offsets one fewer allocation.

Isolated tiny-only cleanup: removed the runtime g_tiny_fused branch and used fixed n=32 packed H/tau views, leaving blocked_qr unchanged. Validation passed, but geomean regressed to 2256.904135 and n=32 was unchanged around 10.295us, so branch cleanup is not useful.

Manager redirect: stopping brief 2 before further tiny/small allocation-return work. Explored packed H/tau return buffers in blocked_qr plus tiny branch cleanup (validated but regressed to 2255.342777) and isolated tiny-only branch cleanup (validated but regressed to 2256.904135). A final restored-parent validation/benchmark had started after restoring the parent file, but the manager redirected before completion/commit; no further iterations were logged. Returning to manager for a new brief focused on top-runtime shapes n=4096, n=2048, mixed n=512, and mixed n=1024.

Target mixed n=1024 batch-60 (14.2% runtime) from baseline by adding per-matrix device classification like the n=512 split win: route well-conditioned matrices through the fast FP16 two-level path and compact only hard matrices into the exact FP32 repair path.

Enabled panel-label classification on the large-low FP16 path so mixed n=1024 can repair flagged matrices exactly, analogous to the n=512 split repair. Validation passed, but geomean regressed to 2257.699730 and mixed n=1024 slowed to 8833us; the detector/repair overhead or over-repair outweighed any accuracy split benefit.

As a split baseline, routed all B=60 n=1024 cases through the exact FP32 large-low two-level path. Validation passed and geomean improved to 2214.835425; mixed n=1024 dropped to 4650.688us (large win), while dense/nearrank n=1024 regressed to ~4656/4662us. This shows the mixed top-shape wants exact repair, but needs a better classifier to avoid hurting dense/nearrank.

Changed n>=1024 bad-matrix repair to the large exact two-level helper and enabled panel-label classification on large-low FP16. Validation passed, but the split overrepaired badly: mixed n=1024 slowed to 7840.768us and geomean regressed to 2258.668608.

Changed existing collinear repair for n>=1024 to use the large exact two-level helper instead of small single-level repair, without panel labels. Validation passed and geomean improved to 2234.896161, but mixed n=1024 remained slow at 7814.541us, so the collinear detector catches costly cases and all-exact B=60 is still better.

Restored the best variant: route all B=60 n=1024 benchmark shapes through exact FP32 large-low two-level QR. Validation passed; final remeasure was 2224.930249 (first run 2214.835425), still a strong improvement over parent 2251.432. Mixed n=1024 improves to ~4.69ms vs ~8.8ms baseline; dense/nearrank n=1024 regress but the mixed top-runtime share dominates.

Mixed n=1024 improves from ~8.8ms to ~4.7ms, while dense/nearrank n=1024 regress to ~4.7ms; net geomean wins due top-runtime mixed share. Tried panel-label split repair and collinear-only large exact repair; both validated but overrepaired or caught costly cases and regressed (2257.699730, 2258.668608, 2234.896161). Captured final nsys profile for mixed n=1024.

Create a lower-build-time landable variant from b1ca555b or 2c67c418: preserve the all-exact B=60 n1024 route and n512 split if cheap, but remove optional classifier/repair machinery that triggers remote timeout, aiming for a remotely accepted score even if local runtime regresses modestly.

Kept compact_collinear removed and large-low FP16 disabled, but restored large-HI n2048 FP16 threshold. Extend current best c430d3ae and explore FP8 more deeply: implement a guarded FP8 trailing GEMM path with per-tile residual-correction pass, targeting dominant trailing-update cost in high-share shapes, avoiding the previously rejected naive FP8 trailing storage conditioning failure and generalizing beyond the narrow INT8-tensor-core Ozaki Gram win.

Added guarded n512 FP8 residual-correction path for W=V^T C: e4m3 quantize W, keep FP16 residual, compute Y=M*(Wq+Wr) with two tensor-core GEMMs. Build passed, regular tests passed, but diff_correctness guard failed n512 mixed/rankdef/clustered shapes with factor residual just over tolerance, so W-only FP8+residual is still too inaccurate for broad n512.

Added guarded FP8 residual-correction for large-low B=60 n1024 FP16 trailing applies: quantize W through e4m3, keep FP16 residual, compute Y=M*Wq + M*Wr with tensor-core GEMMs. Unlike n512, validation and guards passed. Full benchmark metric 2130.556750; dense/nearrank n1024 improved to ~3.98ms, but mixed n1024 stayed ~4.69ms because classifier routes bad mixed matrices exact.

Extended FP8 residual-correction W path to n2048 B=8 large-HI outer applies. Validation and guards passed, but benchmark regressed to 2139.601911 versus n1024-only 2130.556750; n2048 slowed to ~9.25ms, so residual split overhead outweighs any FP8 benefit at B=8.

Extended n1024 FP8-RC to quantize Y with residual before C-=VY as well as W before Y=MW. Validation and guards passed, but metric regressed to 2167.260808; dense/nearrank n1024 slowed to ~4.36ms, so the extra residual pass and second C-update GEMM outweigh reduced precision. W-only FP8-RC remains best.

Restored final HEAD to best brief-5 candidate: guarded n1024 B=60 FP8 residual-correction W path only. Validation and guards passed; benchmark metric 2130.556750. n512 FP8-RC failed guards, n2048 extension validated but regressed to 2139.601911, and Y-side residual correction validated but regressed to 2167.260808.

Recommendation: keep W-only n1024 FP8-RC; future work should pursue true FP8 tensor-core/cublasLt scaled GEMM or a fused residual epilogue, not more split residual GEMMs.

Combine new best 8975f743 with guarded FP8 n1024 residual-correction candidate 0e052c67, preserving n512 one-pass classifier/parallel compile and testing whether the dense/nearrank n1024 FP8 W residual path stacks without hurting mixed exact routing or validation.

Extend current best 8975f743 and target n1024 B=60 mixed exact-route cost by designing a mixed-batch repair path that avoids all-matrix exact FP32: identify hard columns/matrices, run exact QR only on the small bad subset, and fuse scatter/merge to avoid the prior per-matrix split overhead.

Added n1024 B=60 mixed repair path: compact bad matrices, run whole-batch FP16 fast path, exact-FP32 only bad subset, then scatter H/tau repairs. Build, full validation, and guards passed, but benchmark regressed to 2298.367604 because mixed n1024 slowed to 13.03 ms; separate underfilled exact subset plus scatter cost is worse than parent all-matrix exact route. Dense/nearrank n1024 stayed fast around 3.77-3.78 ms.

Added small-subset threshold for n1024 B=60 repair path after diagnostic showed benchmark mixed has 24/60 bad matrices. Repair now only runs for <=8 bad matrices; larger mixed batches fall back to parent all-matrix exact FP32. Build, full validation, and guards passed. Benchmark metric 2111.381608; benchmark mixed n1024 remains exact-route around 4.71 ms, while dense/nearrank n1024 stay fast around 3.78 ms. This preserves safety but does not solve benchmark mixed repair.

Tried replacing custom exact subset QR with torch.geqrf for n1024 B=60 bad-subset repair and allowed all 24/60 mixed bad matrices to repair. Validation and guards passed, but benchmark regressed badly to 2708.418156; mixed n1024 was 93.4 ms, so library geqrf subset is far too slow for the repair role. Will revert to thresholded custom-exact fallback candidate.

Added fused CUDA gather_bad1024/scatter_bad1024 kernels and re-enabled n1024 B=60 mixed repair for all 24/60 bad matrices, replacing PyTorch index_select/index_copy. Build, validation, and guards passed, but benchmark still regressed to 2298.743983 with mixed n1024 at 13.07 ms, essentially same as PyTorch gather/scatter repair. This shows exact subset QR underfill dominates; copy/merge overhead is not the limiting cost.

Brief exhausted. Explored n1024 B=60 mixed-batch repair off current best 8975f743. The input classifier flags 24/60 matrices as bad for benchmark mixed seed 770002, while dense/nearrank flag 0/60. Iteration 1 retained only a safe small-subset repair path (<=8 bad matrices) and falls back to parent all-matrix exact route for 24/60 mixed; validation passed and metric was best at 2111.381608, preserving mixed n1024 around 4.71 ms and dense/nearrank around 3.78 ms, but it does not reduce the benchmark mixed exact-route cost. Iteration 3 fused gather/scatter in CUDA, but mixed repair still ~13.07 ms and metric 2298.743983, proving copy/merge overhead is not the bottleneck; underfilled exact subset QR is. Final HEAD retained 17e5d4a6, the safe thresholded candidate. Further progress likely needs a true batched exact repair kernel that preserves occupancy across only bad matrices or column-level repair inside the FP16 path, not external subset QR plus scatter.

Extend current best 8975f743 and target n1024 B=60 mixed by batching bad matrices into a synthetic full batch for exact QR or using persistent cooperative groups to avoid underfilled subset exact kernels, while preserving dense/nearrank fast routes and validation.

Implemented synthetic full-batch n1024 B=60 repair: compact bad matrices, repeat them into a full B=60 exact-FP32 batch to keep exact kernels occupied, run whole-batch FP16 fast route, then scatter only real bad outputs. Validation and guards passed, but benchmark regressed to 2304.061154; mixed n1024 slowed to 13.56 ms. Filling exact occupancy helps less than the extra FP16 pass plus synthetic copy costs, so this does not beat parent all-FP32 mixed route.

Implemented two synthetic full batches for n1024 B=60 mixed: repeat good matrices into a full FP16 batch and bad matrices into a full exact-FP32 batch, then scatter first good/bad results back. Validation and guards passed; benchmark metric 2226.436032. Mixed n1024 improved versus one-FP16-plus-synthetic-exact repair (8.84 ms vs 13.56 ms) but remains much slower than parent all-matrix exact at ~4.71 ms, so synthetic batching is not enough.

Brief exhausted. Tested synthetic full-batch strategies for n1024 B=60 mixed off current best 8975f743. Iteration 1 used two full synthetic batches, repeating good matrices into a full FP16 batch and bad matrices into a full exact-FP32 batch, then merging; validation/guards passed and mixed n1024 improved to 8.84 ms but still trailed parent all-matrix exact route around 4.71 ms, metric 2226.436032.
